name: Katingan
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.note: Katingan: Glottolog lists only an ISO change request; no descriptive source found

new_statements.quote: a) Tekanan Kata Bersuku satu. Kata bersuku umumnya berupa seruan. Oleh karena itu selalu mendapat tekanan keras. Jika bukan seruan umumnya mendapat tekanan agak keras. [...] b) Tekanan Kata Bersuku Dua. Kata bersuku dua umumnya mendapat tekanan agak keras dan sedang, seperti pada contoh berikut ini. Contoh: [etâŋ] 'keranjang' [tùnîs] 'sunyi' [mètûh] 'sedang' [òmbât] 'mengapa' [tìmbÊn] 'terlalu' c) Tekanan Kata Bersuku Tiga. Kata bersuku tiga umumnya mendapat tekanan agak keras dan sedang. Contoh: [kàwìlâp] 'bilah' [bàgàmbûh] 'rakus' [bàsèpût] 'gemuk' [...] d) Tekanan Kata Bersuku Empat [...] umumnya sedang menuju agak keras. Contoh: [tàbàlîÈn] 'kayu ulin' [...] [kàmàsârày] 'serai' [jàlàtîÈn] 'sembilan'. Berdasarkan data yang diperoleh, dalam bahasa Katingan tidak ditemukan tekanan yang membedakan makna (distingtif).
new_statements.translation: a) Stress in monosyllabic words. Monosyllables are mostly exclamations and therefore always take strong stress; if not exclamations they generally take fairly-strong stress. [...] b) Stress in disyllabic words. Disyllables generally take fairly-strong and medium stress, as in the following examples: [etâŋ] 'basket', [tùnîs] 'quiet', [mètûh] 'medium', [òmbât] 'why', [tìmbÊn] 'too (much)'. c) Stress in trisyllabic words. Trisyllables generally take fairly-strong and medium stress: [kàwìlâp] 'lath', [bàgàmbûh] 'greedy', [bàsèpût] 'fat' [...]. d) Stress in four-syllable words [...] is generally medium moving toward fairly strong: [tàbàlîÈn] 'ironwood', [kàmàsârày] 'lemongrass', [jàlàtîÈn] 'nine'. On the data obtained, no meaning-distinguishing (distinctive) stress is found in Katingan. (Key: [´] strong, [^] fairly strong, [`] medium, [ˇ] weak.)
new_statements.citation: Iper, Dunis; Petrus Poerwadi; Wihadi Admojo. 1998. Fonologi Bahasa Katingan. Jakarta: Pusat Pembinaan dan Pengembangan Bahasa, Departemen Pendidikan dan Kebudayaan. xvi+163 pp. ISBN 979-459-830-5.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is not contrastive. In root words (the stated domain), the strongest non-exclamatory degree ('agak keras', marked ^) sits on the final syllable of every di- and trisyllabic example, with preceding syllables medium; in the few four-syllable roots the ^ mark sits on the penult with a medium final. Monosyllabic exclamations take the top degree. The prose names only the degrees per word length; the locus is read off the authors' diacritics on all 10 two- and three-syllable examples (final) and 5 four-syllable examples (penult).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Non-final syllables of 2-3-syllable roots carry 'tekanan sedang' (medium, marked `); no alternating/rhythmic secondary stress is described.
new_statements.exceptions: Four-syllable roots: main (fairly-strong) mark on the penult, not the final ([tàbàlîÈn], [hàràmâUŋ̀], [kuwaltûtal], [kàmàsârày], [jàlàtîÈn]). Monosyllabic exclamations get the extra-strong degree. Section 2.8.2 adds word pitch contours (2-2, 2-2-3, 2-2-2-2), also non-distinctive.
new_statements.domain_note: Explicitly limited to 'konstruksi kata dasar' (underived root words in citation); nothing on affixed words or phrases. Variety: 'bahasa Katingan dialek Ngawa' (lower Katingan River: Kec. Katingan Hilir, Katingan Tengah, Pulau Malan), chosen as the standard over 'dialek Katingan Ngaju' upriver.
new_statements.identity_note: kati1278 is a Glottolog Bookkeeping languoid for retired ISO [kxg] Katingan, merged in 2008 into Ngaju [nij] (ngaj1237); Glottolog's ngaj1237 has no Katingan dialect node (children: Ba'amang, Mantangai, Pulopetak). The source describes 'bahasa Katingan dialek Ngawa', the lower-Katingan-River variety (Kec. Katingan Hilir, Katingan Tengah, Pulau Malan, Central Kalimantan), which the authors themselves, citing Poerwadi 1992 (86% lexicostatistic agreement), regard as a dialect of Ngaju. Its stress marking (final in 2-3-syllable roots) differs from the held Kahayan sketch (Durasid et al. 1990: 2nd syllable from word start) and from the general Ngaju sources held under ngaj1237 (penult), so it should be filed as a Katingan-Ngawa dialect point under ngaj1237 rather than merged with those statements. Do not confuse with kati1270 (Kati, Nuristani), whose folder sits next to this one.
